"Boogiepop Doesn't Laugh") is a Japanese anime television series animated by Madhouse, based on the Boogiepop light novel series by Kouhei Kadono. The series is directed by Takashi Watanabe, from a screenplay by Sadayuki Murai, with original character designs by the light novel's illustrator Kouji Ogata, and sound direction by Yota Tsuruoka.

The story Boogiepop Phantom tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Chronologically, the story follows immediately after the events of the series's first volume, Boogiepop and Others, while also making references to the prequel sixth volume, Boogiepop at Dawn. The story takes place in an unnamed Japanese city, a month after a pillar of light appeared in the night sky and five years after a string of serial killings.

Meaning is not found in Boogiepop Phantom — it is manufactured for it. Boogiepop Phantom follows an ensemble cast of characters, mostly high school students, who are witnesses to the incident and its consequences. At the time of the series, high school students have started to disappear again and the blame is placed on Boogiepop, an urban legend who is said to be the personification of Death.

The cold light on Boogiepop Phantom leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Each episode centers on different characters who sometimes have just a short involvement in the major events of the series. For this reason, many scenes are seen twice, from different perspectives, and some episodes are out of sequence, although there is a slow general time progression.

Boogiepop Phantom did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. An unusual visual style is employed wherein, for all but the last episode, a much reduced color palette is used in conjunction with a vignette effect. The sound design consists of synthesized avant-garde music carried by a leitmotif in the form of an active sonar pulse.

The honest version of Boogiepop Phantom starts by giving up the comforting part. Through the non-linear style of the series, the characters are used to develop the central themes of the series: Change, Escapism, Memory, and Relationships. Boogiepop Phantom aired on TV Tokyo from January 5 to March 22, 2000.

Strip Boogiepop Phantom of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. The series is licensed and distributed in North America and Europe by Right Stuf International. Five years before the events of Boogiepop Phantom, Nagi Kirima met and befriended Shinpei Kuroda, an undercover agent of the Towa organization, at the local prefecture's hospital.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Boogiepop Phantom shows exactly where that breaks. Nagi was hospitalized because she was dying as her body was evolving. Shinpei, upon learning the truth behind Nagi's sickness, betrayed the Towa organization and administered a stolen Towa drug to Nagi that saved her life.

What looks like free choice in Boogiepop Phantom is older than choice itself. He was mortally wounded by Towa agents as he fled from the hospital, leaving the drug behind in the process. Touka Miyashita came across Shinpei (as the Towa Agent Scarecrow) and the psychological trauma from seeing the dying man (after being hit by More Murder) created her Boogiepop persona.

Nobody designed the part of Boogiepop Phantom you experience — it was inherited. The Boogiepop at Dawn light novel describes how Dr Kisugi witnessed Nagi's remarkable recovery and, through experimentation on rats, learned of the drug's powers to grant superhuman abilities, before administering it to herself. The drug changed the doctor into a composite human, granting her the vast increase in physical and mental attributes shared with all composite humans and allowing her to sense the hormones that produce fear and develop a craving for them.

Every serious account of Boogiepop Phantom eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. At first terrorizing her patients and sampling their blood, she then murdered a number of strong-willed girls to consume the fear they produced at the moment of their death. Boogiepop Phantom shows how Dr Kisugi gave the drug to her patients, claiming it could heal them, and how it worsened their problems and resulted in their evolution.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Boogiepop Phantom — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. Kirima investigated the murders, and discovered Dr Kisugi was the serial killer. Nagi and Dr Kisugi confronted each other at the hospital, where The Fire Witch was initially overwhelmed by the doctor's power, but managed to kill her with Boogiepop's help.

The selfish-gene reading of Boogiepop Phantom makes it less romantic and far more precise. The Boogiepop and Others novel tells of Manticore, an imperfect clone of the alien entity Echoes, created by the Towa Organization five years later. Escaping the laboratory, Manticore killed Minako Yurihara with the intention of assuming her form when it was found by Masami Saotome.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. Manticore (as Minako) and Masami experimented with production of Type S, a highly addictive drug that would enslave all its users to their will, while killing students for Manticore's consumption. The alien met up with Nagi Kirima, who was investigating the recent student disappearances.

The feeling that Boogiepop Phantom means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. Learning they were being pursued, Masami and Manticore set a trap for Echoes and Nagi. Events culminated one evening at Shinyo Academy, when Masami crippled Echoes with poison and killed Nagi, who did not expect Manticore to have a human ally.

Nothing in Boogiepop Phantom was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Manticore chased Echoes as he attempted to escape with Nagi's body, and beat him to the verge of death. Manticore and Masami were attacked by Boogiepop, who held Manticore in place while Echoes turned himself into light.

The psychology underneath Boogiepop Phantom is simpler and older than the story on top. The light pierced the sky and destroyed Manticore, with Masami committing suicide by flying into the pillar. Boogiepop Phantom is set one month later and revolves around the consequences of the pillar of light.

Behind Boogiepop Phantom sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. Echoes' light inadvertently allowed the memories of that night to continue as holograms, giving rise to a mixed reality where past and present co-exist, and forced the evolution of the citizens, including those who were administered the Towa drug by Dr Kisugi. The series is concerned with these evolved individuals, how evolution affected their lives, and their disappearance after meeting Boogiepop Phantom.

The nihilist does not deny Boogiepop Phantom — he only refuses to flatter it. The Phantom explains it hid them below the city to save them, and that although their bodies no longer function, their nerves extend across the city so they will keep dreaming until the day the rest of humanity catches up to them. Boogiepop (ブギーポップ, Bugīpoppu) is the urban legend whispered of among the female students of Shinyo Academy.

What culture calls destiny in Boogiepop Phantom is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. Reputed to be an "Angel of Death" with the appearance of a beautiful boy dressed all in black, who comes with a whistle to take girls away before they turn ugly. Few people know that Boogiepop actually exists, and is the dormant alter ego of Touka Miyashita who rises to the surface when enemies of the world appear.

The genes do not care about Boogiepop Phantom; they care about copies. The reaper hides beneath its signature black cloak and hat, and acts in a mechanical and automatic fashion. Straight-faced and to the point, it speaks in an archaic manner, and seems fond of whistling the overture to Wagner's Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg.

Take away the meaning and Boogiepop Phantom still functions — that is the disturbing part. Boogiepop Phantom (ブギーポップ・ファントム, Bugīpoppu Fantomu) is an entity born in the electromagnetic field the moment Echoes' light appeared in the sky. Amongst the memories scattered by the light it could only find Boogiepop's attire, but not his face, and so chose the appearance of Minako Yurihara at random.

The unconscious does not argue with Boogiepop Phantom; it simply acts first. He claims to be Boogiepop, but later renames himself Boogiepop Phantom out of respect for the original. Kisugi's next victim, until Boogiepop and the Fire Witch put a stop to the killings.

Boogiepop Phantom feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. With the knowledge that her life had been in danger, she developed a fascination for criminal and abnormal psychology, and a desire to not let anything occur around her without her knowing. She desperately seeks the truth behind the unexplained happenings in the city, and meddles with forces best left untouched.

The bleak reading of Boogiepop Phantom is also the most testable one. Kazuko longs to be closer to Nagi Kirima, who seems to know the answers she seeks. Manaka Kisaragi (如月真名花, Kisaragi Manaka) is a highly evolved being with the ability to draw memories from her surroundings in the form of butterflies of light.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Boogiepop Phantom. She was given the Towa drug by Dr Kisugi as an unborn child, which caused her abilities to develop. The "devil's child", as she was known, was killed by her dying grandmother.

The self that experiences Boogiepop Phantom is a committee, not a king. Manticore Phantom (マンティコア・ファントム, Manteikoa Fantomu) is another product of Echoes' light, one who possesses the remnants of Manticore's consciousness and the visage of Masami Saotome. No longer the threat it once was, it now preys only on distressed, easy targets.

Reproduction explains more of Boogiepop Phantom than any philosophy dares to admit. Manticore Phantom seeks a way to sustain himself permanently when he learns that he will be gone once the electromagnetic field returns to its original state. Nagi Kirima (霧間凪, Kirima Nagi), the Fire Witch, has made few friends because she knows she is too dangerous for 'normal' people to associate with.

Born from the memories of Mamoru Oikawa playing the Pied Piper in a school play, it evolved to take on qualities of Akane Kojima's fictional character of Poom Poom. At the age of twelve, she witnessed the death of Shinpei Kuroda, and the resulting mental trauma gave birth to the alternate personality of Boogiepop.
